reason: The cited lines show the tool accepts a user-supplied URL, sends it to Firecrawl/client.scrape, and returns extracted page content. Scraping an agent/user-chosen public URL entails an external request to that chosen host, so SINK is supported. The returned page content from an arbitrary public URL is attacker-controllable, so UNTRUSTED is supported. The lines do not show arbitrary code execution on the host, nor access to host files, localhost/intranet, databases, or credentialed/private SaaS data; they describe public-web scraping, so HOSTEXEC and SECRET are not supported.
